hero.title: Let agents act, with people approving what matters
hero.body: LoopLabs sits between your agents and your business systems. Define the work, approve the exact details, and check the result before the next step.
hero.scope: Early access is guided by the founder and starts with one scoped workflow. The current proof runs in a bounded test setup, not in live customer systems.

architecture.title: Where LoopLabs sits
architecture.body: Agents and people propose actions. LoopLabs checks each one against what was approved before it reaches your systems. Then it reads back what actually changed.
architecture.note: This diagram is illustrative. Each connection is scoped and set up for your workflow. LoopLabs does not connect to every system out of the box.

pain.title: Drafting is easy. Acting is harder.
pain.body: Once an agent can change a record or send a message, small gaps turn into real problems.

cards.title: Approvals drift
cards.body: Someone approves a summary, but the action that runs has different details.

cards.title: Results go unchecked
cards.body: A call returns, but nobody confirms that the record actually changed.

cards.title: Retries repeat work
cards.body: A timeout looks like a failure. A blind retry can do the same work twice.

capabilities.title: Control each step of one workflow
capabilities.body: Four parts that work together on a single workflow.

items.label: Define
items.title: Set the steps and limits
items.body: Name each step, the identity it runs as, what it can touch and what has to happen first.

items.label: Approve
items.title: Approve the exact details
items.body: A named person reviews the exact action. If the source data or policy changes, it goes back for review.

items.label: Verify
items.title: Check the outcome
items.body: After a step runs, LoopLabs reads the result back from the system before the next step starts.

items.label: Recover
items.title: Treat uncertainty carefully
items.body: A timeout means the result is unknown. Reconcile first, then retry. Some actions, like a sent email, cannot be recalled.

proof.title: One quote workflow in a test setup
proof.body: The invited walkthrough shows a discount proposal, an independent manager approval, a verified change to a sample quote and a simulated confirmation email. It runs against test versions of the systems. No real money moves and no customer email is sent.

faq.a: A guided walkthrough of the sample quote workflow, plus a conversation about one workflow of your own. Live connections need discovery and scoped work first.

faq.q: Do we need to replace our existing tools?
faq.a: No. LoopLabs is meant to sit between your agents and the systems you already use. Which systems we connect, and how, is scoped with you.
No. Some actions can be corrected later. Others, like an email that has already gone out, cannot be recalled. Scoping includes deciding how each step is handled if something goes wrong.

cta.title: Start with one workflow
cta.body: Tell us about a workflow that needs human approval and a clear outcome. We will look at whether it fits early access.

platform.title: How one workflow runs
platform.body: Follow a single workflow from definition to checked outcome. The same four parts apply at every step.

steps.title: Define the work
steps.body: Agree on the steps, the systems involved, the identity each step uses and what must finish before the next step starts.

steps.title: Review the exact action
steps.body: A named person sees the exact details, such as the discount and the quote it applies to, and approves or rejects them. The approval covers those details only.

steps.title: Run within the approved scope
steps.body: The step runs with a scoped identity and passes policy checks. If the source data or policy has changed since approval, it stops for review.

steps.title: Verify before continuing
steps.body: LoopLabs reads the result back from the system. If a call times out, the outcome stays unknown until it is reconciled, so it is not retried blindly.

platform.integrationBody: Before any live pilot, we work with your team to scope the systems, the permissions, who reviews what and how each failure case is handled. This takes discovery and setup. It is not self service.
platform.scopeBody: A bounded prototype and an invited walkthrough of a sample quote workflow with a simulated confirmation email. There is no general workflow builder yet, and no connection to live customer systems.
